raw_case_text:
A 36-year-old man presented to the outpatient department with jaundice for 1.5 months along with pain in the right upper quadrant for 1 week. There was no history of loss of appetite, weight loss, fever, or melena. He denied comorbidities and was a temporary resident of Kashmir, the northern most state of India, situated in the Himalayan foothills. On examination, the abdomen was soft and non-tender. A hard mass was palpable in the right upper quadrant. The abdominal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) revealed a large solid-cystic intrahepatic lesion measuring 125x118x123 mm involving the hepatic segments IV, VII, and VIII (Figure 1). 
This lesion showed peripheral subtle curvilinear and central nodular calcification. Arterial phase images revealed mild peripheral enhancement, while mild delayed phase enhancement was also noted. This lesion was found to compress the left portal vein and right main bile duct, causing right intrahepatic biliary radicle dilatation (IHBRD). Small cystic lesions were noted involving both lobes of the liver, the largest measuring 23x18 mm, and a few enlarged periportal lymph nodes (the largest measuring 18x14mm). The positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET-CT) revealed peripherally FDG-avid necrotic lesions with central calcification. His peripheral blood investigations showed a mild eosinophil increase (9%) with normal hemoglobin and total leukocyte count. The liver function test revealed mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, mild transaminase elevation, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and a reversed albumin: globulin ratio (Table 1). His serum CEA, CA-19-9, and AFP levels were within normal limits.
A clinical possibility of a multifocal/metastatic centrally necrotizing malignant mass versus alveolar hydatid disease was considered, and a liver biopsy was performed. The liver biopsy highlighted multiple randomly dispersed foci of eosinophilic necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes, a pale zone of fibrosis, and a thick collar of lymphocytes at places (Figures 2A and 2B). These foci of necrosis were dominantly lobular, at places confluent, giving rise to large necrotic areas. A few foci contained pale, refractile eosinophilic membranes, which were strongly PAS-positive (Figures 2C and 2D). No tumor was seen. This morphology was classical to alveolar echinococcosis.
The intervening portal tracts and the lobules showed variable degrees of inflammatory cell infiltration containing lymphocytes and occasional eosinophils. The individual is planned for surgical resection alongside treatment with anthelminthic agents.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old man presented with jaundice for 1.5 months and right upper quadrant abdominal pain for 1 week.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed progressive jaundice over 1.5 months followed by right upper quadrant abdominal pain for 1 week prior to outpatient presentation.
subjective.past_medical_history: No medical comorbidities; temporary resident of Kashmir in the Himalayan foothills of northern India.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for jaundice and right upper quadrant pain; negative for anorexia, weight loss, fever, or melena.

objective.physical_examination: Abdomen was soft and non-tender with a hard palpable mass in the right upper quadrant.
objective.routine_investigations: Peripheral blood workup showed mild eosinophilia (9%) with normal hemoglobin and total leukocyte count. Liver function tests showed mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, mildly elevated transaminases, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and a reversed albumin:globulin ratio. Serum CEA, CA 19-9, and AFP were within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CECT revealed a large 125 x 118 x 123 mm solid-cystic intrahepatic mass in segments IV, VII, and VIII with peripheral curvilinear and central nodular calcifications, mild peripheral arterial and delayed enhancement, compression of the left portal vein and right main bile duct with right intrahepatic biliary radicle dilatation, bilateral small satellite hepatic cysts (up to 23 x 18 mm), and enlarged periportal lymph nodes (up to 18 x 14 mm). FDG PET-CT showed peripherally FDG-avid necrotic lesions with central calcification. Liver biopsy histopathology demonstrated multiple confluent lobular foci of eosinophilic necrosis containing strongly PAS-positive pale refractile laminated membranes surrounded by palisading histiocytes, fibrosis, and a lymphocytic collar with eosinophils and no malignancy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Hepatic alveolar echinococcosis, definitively confirmed by liver biopsy histopathology showing PAS-positive refractile eosinophilic laminated membranes within necrotizing granulomas (ruling out multifocal/metastatic hepatic malignancy). The patient was planned for surgical hepatic resection combined with anthelmintic therapy.
